# Keel

> Keel is a Rust framework that owns everything under the pixels of native iOS, Android and web apps: domain logic, reactive state, the data layer, persistence and the dev loop. It generates idiomatic Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript from one Rust core, and the UI stays SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose and React. Not to be confused with keel.sh (Kubernetes) or keel.so.

Keel is open source (MIT OR Apache-2.0) and ships a `keel` CLI (`keel init`, `keel dev`, `keel build`, `keel bindgen`, `keel doctor`). Reads never cross the language boundary: each platform holds a mirror of the state, updated by one binary change-set per transaction.

## Docs

- [Keel documentation](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/): Guides and reference for Keel, the Rust framework for native iOS, Android and web apps: getting started, concepts, queries, ports, the CLI and the API.
- [Getting started · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/getting-started.html): Install the Keel CLI with brew, npm, curl or cargo, scaffold a project, run the live dev loop and run the app on iOS, Android and the web.
- [Core concepts · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/concepts.html): Stores, signals, computeds, transactions, change-sets and keyed lists, and why a list write costs the change and not the list.
- [Queries & mutations · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/queries.html): The data layer in the core: cached queries with staleness and dedup, retry, optimistic mutations with precise rollback, persistence and an offline queue.
- [Ports & adapters · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/ports.html): The ten standard ports, the default adapter on each platform, how to supply your own, what happens when one is missing, and the fakes for tests.
- [The CLI · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/cli.html): Every keel command and flag, the keel.toml project file, exit codes and how errors are reported.
- [Architecture · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/architecture.html): How Keel is built: the schema, generators, runtimes, wire format and C ABI, the threading model, diagnostics, and the twelve rules every change follows.
- [API overview, Swift · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/api-swift.html): What Keel's generated Swift looks like: records, enums, errors, objects, stores, query handles and ports, and how the KeelRuntime package loads the core.
- [API overview, Kotlin · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/api-kotlin.html): What Keel's generated Kotlin looks like: data classes, sealed types, suspend functions, StateFlow-backed stores, query handles and ports.
- [API overview, TypeScript · Keel docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/docs/api-typescript.html): What Keel's generated TypeScript looks like: interfaces, unions, error classes, promise-returning stores with signals, React hooks and adapters.

## Roadmap

- [Keel roadmap: shipped, now, next and later](https://shreypdev.github.io/keel/roadmap/): The Keel roadmap: what shipped in v1.0, what is in flight for v1.x, what is planned next and what is on the horizon. Updated with the project record.
